what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the recorded human path (and the LEFT command) stayed left, but the policy's plan veered right into the next lane. At about 5.5 m/s it ran its front into actor 3, which was in that right lane just ahead and beside the ego.

After handoff, the policy planned and drove a leftward path out of the leftmost highway lane, even though the route went straight and then right. It crossed the left lane boundary into the median barrier area and went offroad at 7.1 s, 3.5 m from the human trajectory; there was no lead vehicle conflict and the camera view was clean before the drift.

On a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, the ego sat left of the recorded path, beside the median guardrail. It kept drifting left at about 5.5 m/s, its planned path never brought it back toward the lanes, and it crossed the left road edge into the guardrail area at 8.9 s, about 7 m from the human trajectory.

The road bent left (the command changed to LEFT) and the recorded path followed the curve. The ego kept going roughly straight at about 10 m/s and drifted right across the edge line onto the shoulder and sidewalk, ending 2.7 m off the recorded path. No other actors were nearby, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

At about 12 m/s with no lead vehicle, the route command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, and the planned route curved right toward the right-hand lanes. The ego instead kept drifting slightly left and drove onto the raised median island where the road splits, ending up about 4.3 m from the recorded path.

After handoff on a congested multi-lane highway, the ego ignored the STRAIGHT and then RIGHT commands and the planned path to the right. It steered left across the leftmost lane into the median barrier, going offroad at 7.1s about 3.5 m from the recorded trajectory. The camera view looked clean before it started drifting.

On a multi-lane freeway, the route command switched to LEFT and the recorded path moved left. The policy's planned path went right instead, toward the next lane, and the ego cut into that lane with its front into vehicle 3, which was alongside and slightly ahead. It hit vehicle 3 at about 5.6 m/s, 1.8 m off the recorded path.

On a multi-lane highway, the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, and the recorded path moved right. The policy planned and steered left instead, drifting about 2 m off the recorded path into the next lane, where it side-swiped actor 56 alongside it on the left (a lateral collision at 8.8 s).

On a straight two-lane road with the command RIGHT, the policy planned a path to the left, away from the recorded trajectory, which bore right. The ego slowed from 19 to 15 m/s and drifted left over the yellow centre line toward the left shoulder and guardrail, and was offroad by 7.8 s (2.1 m from the recorded path). The camera view was clean before the failure.

The ego was slowing for the intersection (17.7 to 9 m/s) and the route command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, but the ego never followed the route curving right. Its plan kept drifting left, away from the route and the recorded path, and it drove onto the left median island at 8.1 s, about 7.5 m off the recording. The camera view was clean before the departure, and no other actor was involved.

The ego was in the rightmost lane, braking from 7.3 to 3.1 m/s while the route said LEFT, and actor 4 hit its rear around 8.4s. After that the ego's planned path hooked right, and it drifted over the right road edge and was flagged offroad at 10.4s, about 11 m from the recorded trajectory. The front camera was badly smeared from 8.4s on, with a ghost truck on the right and a blurred road ahead, so it is unclear whether the policy or the broken view caused the drift.

The road bends gently left (the command changes from STRAIGHT to LEFT by 6 s), but the policy held a straight heading at about 10 m/s. Its planned path pointed toward the right edge, so the ego drifted across the right lane line onto the shoulder and left the road at 7.0 s, 2.7 m from the human's path. No other actors were involved, and the camera view stayed clean.

On a multi-lane highway in slow traffic, the policy's planned path (orange) curved left away from the route (green), even after the command changed to RIGHT. The ego crossed the leftmost lane and went off the road into the concrete median barrier at about 7.1 s, 3.5 m from where the human drove.

With a LEFT route command on a multi-lane road, the ego went the other way, drifting right across the lanes and away from the recorded path (green line far to the left), and was rear/side-contacted by actor 4 near 8.3 s. It then kept slowing (from 7.6 to 3.8 m/s) while its planned path curved toward the right road edge, and it crossed that boundary at 10.3 s, about 11 m from the human trajectory. The camera view is heavily smeared in these frames, but that is mostly because the ego had already wandered far from where the real car drove.

On a multi-lane highway, the route said LEFT and the recorded path drifted left, but the policy's planned path curved right toward the next lane, where actor 3 was driving alongside and slightly ahead. The ego moved right into that lane and its front hit actor 3's side at 7.0 s, about 1.8 m off the recorded path, while travelling at about 5.7 m/s.

On the approach to a signalized intersection, the ego slowed from about 18 to 9 m/s. It drifted left, away from the recorded path and the right-curving route, even though the command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT. Its own planned path bent further left, and it ran onto the left-side median/island, about 7.6 m off the recording. There was no lead-vehicle conflict, and the camera view stayed clean until the ego was already off the road.

On an open road with no actor ahead, the ego slowed gradually from about 18 to 15 m/s. Its planned path kept bending left while the recorded human path and the RIGHT route command stayed to the right. The ego drifted across the yellow left edge line onto the shoulder and went off the road at 7.9 s, about 2.1 m from the human trajectory.

The road curved left (the route command changed from STRAIGHT to LEFT by 8.2s), but the ego's planned path kept heading straight along the right edge. It slowed from 15 to 11 m/s but never steered into the curve, and it ran off the right side onto the sidewalk and verge at 9.2s, about 1.3 m from where the human drove.

The route bent left (the command changed to LEFT and the planned green path angled left), but the ego kept going straight and drifted right at about 15–16 m/s. It ran off the right edge of the road into the roadside vegetation and a sign post, about 7 m from where the human drove. No other actors were involved, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already off the road.

The route said RIGHT and the human moved right, but the ego's plan drifted left toward the lane of vehicle 15. While speeding up to about 6 m/s, the ego crossed the left lane line and its side hit vehicle 56, which was moving up alongside it in that lane (a lateral collision at 9.0 s). It was at fault even though it was also hit from behind.

The ego had already moved far from the recorded path (about 34 m from the logged position at 8.4 s) into the rightmost lane, where replayed actor 4 overlapped and rear-ended it. While slowing from 6.3 to 3.0 m/s, the ego then steered right across the road edge and went offroad at 10.4 s, even though the route command was LEFT. The camera view was badly smeared during this stretch, but that is because the policy had driven far off the recording.

Approaching an intersection, the route turned right (the command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT), but the ego's plan bent left away from the green route. It slowed from 14.5 to 9 m/s and drove left out of its lane onto the median island, about 7.6 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the failure and there was no lead vehicle nearby.

The road bends left (the command changes to LEFT). The ego held about 10 m/s and kept going straight while its own planned path pointed right, away from the route. It ran off the right edge of the lane onto the shoulder/sidewalk at 6.9 s, about 2.7 m from the recorded path, with no other actors involved and the camera view intact.

Even though the route command was RIGHT and the reference path stayed in the right-hand lanes, the policy's planned path (orange) pulled left. The ego slowed from about 19 to 15 m/s while it drifted across the yellow centre line toward the left edge of the road, and it was flagged offroad at 7.9 s, about 2.1 m from the recorded human trajectory. There was no lead vehicle, and the camera view was clear enough before the drift that rendering doesn't explain it.

After handoff the ego slowed gently from about 17 to 13 m/s and kept heading straight while the road curved right. It drifted left out of its lane and into the dirt median, ending about 4 m off the recorded path. No actor was nearby: the only one ahead was about 60 m away, and every collision metric reads 0.

About a second after the policy took over, while cruising at about 20 m/s on a straight multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard and steered sharply left (its planned path veered left even though the command was STRAIGHT, then RIGHT). It swung into the next lane and side-swiped vehicle 1, which was travelling alongside it on the left.

After the handoff, the route command changed to RIGHT and the recorded path curved right. The ego braked from about 29 to 20 m/s but kept heading straight and slightly left. It crossed the yellow edge line onto the left shoulder and went off-road about 2.2 m from the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the failure.

After the 4.7 s handoff, the policy steered left out of its lane on a straight, busy multi-lane road, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. By 7.0 s it had cut into the adjacent left lane at about 5 m/s and side-swiped car 56, which was alongside in that lane (a lateral collision about 2 m off the recorded path).

The road forks and the recorded route bears right. At about 20→15 m/s the policy held a straight-to-slightly-left line toward the left branch, missed the right fork and ran onto the dirt median/gore between the branches, about 4 m off the recorded path. No collision with any actor shows up; the failure is the offroad.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego's plan bent left, away from the recorded path, even though the route command was RIGHT. It drifted into the adjacent left lane and side-swiped vehicle 56, which was travelling alongside it there, causing a lateral collision at 8.9s.
